the lipid headgroups interact with a conserved charged motif within LmrP that controls the conformational equilibria through an electrostatic mechanism.

the lipids modulate the dynamics of the transporter by direct interaction with the charged residues of the conserved motif, which is in turn crucial for the conformational equilbrium and hence the function of the protein.

the lipid headgroups of the lipid bilayer modulate the con formational equilibrium of a secondary multidr ug transporter through an electrostatic interplay within the protein, which is mediated by a conserved motif.

The main takeaway from our work is that

lipid headgroups directly affect the conformational energy landscape of a membrane protein, through an interplay between the electrostatics within the protein and the electrostatics of the lipid headgroups.
the lipid headgroups of the bilayer directly interact with a conserved motif in the protein, thereby modulating the conformational landscape of the transporter.

lipids are not just passive scaffolds, but rather actively shape the conformation of membrane proteins, and that this is achieved by direct interactions of lipid headgroups with specific protein motifs.
